context.body: Luke narrates John’s imprisonment before briefly reporting Jesus’ baptism.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The word of God comes to John in a named political and priestly setting; he announces repentance, answers crowds, and denies being the Christ.
observations.label: Luke dates John’s call and records its social demands: action

observations.body: John names concrete fruits, the coming stronger one, Spirit and fire, good news, and Herod’s imprisonment.
observations.label: Luke dates John’s call and records its social demands: response

observations.body: word of God · repentance · fruits · Christ · Spirit and fire
observations.label: Words in Luke 3:1–20

payload.posture: Read Luke 3:1–20 as john prepares the way evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Narrative placement does not by itself state that imprisonment occurred before Jesus was baptized.
payload.title: Luke dates John’s call and records its social demands
